U.S. policy toward Cuba is about to change. How and to what extent it'll change is less clear. But we know that the White House will issue its review of US Cuba policy in June, most likely in the middle or the end of the month. In the meantime, various bills to keep lifting restrictions against the island are gaining support. Such is a case with the agricultural exports bill, Arkansas Representative Rick Crawford first introduced to Congress in 2015. Crawford has since made some changes to it, after working with congressmen opposed to re-establishing U.S. Cuba ties. I'm Elizabeth Gonzalez from ASCOA Online. And after a year since I last spoke to congressmen Crawford, I circled back to see what this new compromise means for Americans and Cuban Americans and how the mood is changing from Washington to Cuba and more. Thank you so much, Mr. Congressman, for taking the time to date.

Well, basically, it's the same bill that we talked about last year with one added compromise that was at the request of Congressman Carbello. And it is a 2% fee on the transactions that would take place in agricultural sales. And so basically, that 2% would go to liquidating the claims of certified claimants, degrees, Cuban Americans who had lost, had property fees and had certified claims. And so that money would be administered by the Treasury Department. Once it was collected, it would go to liquidate the claims. Burying numbers of, I've heard anywhere from $3 billion in outstanding certified claims to maybe even as high as $8 billion. I'm not sure exactly what the number is, but obviously it would be capped so that it's not a fee that would be going on indefinitely, but once claims are liquidated, then that fee would go away.
Okay. And this is a bill that still isn't before Congress,

right? Right. Well, HR 525 is, but what we did, what we're, you know, working with our friends in South Florida is at the, what we call the Cabello Compromise, which put the language in that provides the 2% transaction fee to go toward the liquidation of those certified claims.
